name: Amariah
overview: The name Amariah appears multiple times in Scripture as a significant priestly figure, often connected to Levitical lineage and temple service. Notably, Amariah is identified as a chief priest during King Jehoshaphat's reign, entrusted with overseeing matters of the LORD, demonstrating a leadership role in spiritual governance (2 Chronicles 19:11). Additionally, genealogical records highlight Amariah as the father of Ahitub, linking him within a priestly family line (1 Chronicles 6:7, 6:11, 6:52). The references to Amariah among the sons of Hebron further emphasize his Levite heritage and role in temple duties (1 Chronicles 23:19, 24:23). Together, these passages reveal Amariah as a faithful servant in the priesthood, exemplifying the continuity of God's appointed leadership in Israel's worship.
